clue.text: Live in big apartment

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so one piece is wrapped by the other

parts.note: big as in stout or large
L marks the live terminal on a British electric plug

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a spacious home, living in a big apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: British plugs label their terminals L (live), N (neutral) and E (earth), which is where L for live comes from; it goes inside FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a flat is a self-contained set of rooms on one floor, the everyday synonym for an apartment.

clue.text: Word of warning by man on board where the crew is housed

parts.note: the cry a golfer shouts to warn others of a ball in flight
a chessman, a piece on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A warning shout from a sailor aboard ship, near the crew's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor, but the board is a chessboard and the man is a chess piece, the castle or rook.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship below deck, traditionally the sailors' living quarters.

clue.text: Useful thing, when fixed

parts.note: as in 'as I arrived', meaning when
set means settled or fixed in place

explanation.surface: Something only becomes useful once it has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable or advantageous resource, so a useful thing in general terms.

clue.text: Bullion is secure inside plant

parts.note: bullion is gold or silver in bars

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the letters of the word next to it

parts.note: taken as written
to lock is to make secure

explanation.surface: Gold bars are safely locked away inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, but it is a flower: a wild buttercup that shares its name with the fairy-tale girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldilocks is a name for a wild buttercup species, a yellow-flowered woodland plant.

clue.text: Speech from leader of Opposition on fixed allowance

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
a ration is a fixed portion allotted to each person

explanation.surface: The Opposition leader gives a speech about fixed allowances.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so O sits on top of RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public speech, delivered on a ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: One inside discourages people trying to lose weight

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the letters of the word next to it

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something inside a person puts off would-be slimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieters restrict their food intake in an effort to shed weight, which is what slimmers do.

clue.text: Stranded, like Noah on Ararat?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, literal: the ark grounded on a mountain top as the flood waters drained

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: after the flood Noah's ark came to rest on Mount Ararat, both up on a height and out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stranded or abandoned in a helpless position, like a boat beached when the tide goes out.

clue.text: Unanimity shown by clubs regarding count, we're told

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
on means about or concerning

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a census is an official count of the population

explanation.surface: A golf club's members all agree on how to count something.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general agreement among a group, which at its fullest is unanimity.

clue.text: Small old house in part of central London

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
O is a standard abbreviation for old
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A tiny old cottage tucked away in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of London's West End known for its restaurants, clubs and theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a named district in the West End of central London.

clue.text: Timidest trembling with nerves in ballet interlude

indicators.note: trembling letters are shaken up and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two words of fodder

explanation.surface: The shyest dancer shakes with stage fright during a ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertissement is a short dance episode inserted into a ballet, a diversion from the main plot.

clue.text: Understood about blocking wily subterfuge to send down student

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it

parts.note: a ruse is a cunning trick

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word runs right to left

parts.note: tacit means understood without being stated

explanation.surface: A tacit understanding foils a cunning plan to expel a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' is the British university phrase for expelling or suspending a student.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, to rusticate a student is to suspend them temporarily from the university as a punishment.

clue.text: Bird in church, by font, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A bird has got into a church and perched by the baptismal font.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in the order F, IN, CH, though the clue lists the font last.
explanation.definitionFit: The finch is a small seed-eating songbird, such as the chaffinch or goldfinch.

clue.text: Somehow wealthier, hence can afford firework

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are arranged by no fixed plan

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being better off, someone can now pay for fireworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can afford' here means gives, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework pinned to a post, named after the saint's wheel of martyrdom.

clue.text: Promise action

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a formal agreement or pledge, as to marry
second meaning: a battle or fight between forces

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a pairing of word and deed, but each is a separate meaning of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a pledge, especially to marry, and a military clash between armies.

clue.text: Tense, we brewed, and put in sugar

indicators.note: brewed things are mixed and stewed together, so the letters come out recombined

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling anxious, we made a pot of tea and added sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten a drink or dish is to add sugar or another sweet ingredient to it.

clue.text: Human organ — length shown in article

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

indicators.note: shown in means displayed within, so one piece is set inside another

parts.note: an article is a thing or object
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A body part has been measured and put on display in a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a grammatical word such as 'a', but here it is a general noun for an object.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction an earthling is a person from Earth, a human being as seen by aliens.

clue.text: Employs symbols in operation

parts.note: signs are symbols
on means working or in operation

explanation.surface: A system that runs by using symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign someone on is to take them on as an employee or crew member.

clue.text: Mrs Dalloway caught out in Greek city

indicators.note: out means removed or dropped from the name

parts.note: Clarissa Dalloway is the heroine of Virginia Woolf's novel
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Virginia Woolf's heroine is caught unawares during a trip to Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Dalloway's first name is Clarissa; drop its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Larissa is the capital of the Thessaly region in central Greece, a sizeable city.

clue.text: Judge arrives carrying snack

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it within, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
a bite is a quick snack

explanation.surface: A judge turns up at court with a packed lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person who settles a dispute, someone appointed to judge between parties.

clue.text: Perhaps pens article about Ecstasy in Welsh city

parts.note: a pen is a female swan; perhaps signals an example

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the pair is read in the opposite order

parts.note: the indefinite article
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Pens and a newspaper piece about a drug in a Welsh city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writing tools but means female swans.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is the second-largest city in Wales, on the south coast.

clue.text: More than one buckler, maybe, is held awkwardly on set, at first

indicators.note: held awkwardly means gripped clumsily and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prop shield is gripped clumsily on a film set at the start of filming.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small round shield, so several bucklers are one example of shields; 'maybe' marks that.

clue.text: Children bet me I misinterpreted nursery rhyme

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so the letters are taken in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Children wager that the speaker got a nursery rhyme wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Three Blind Mice is a traditional English nursery rhyme and round about a farmer's wife and her carving knife.

clue.text: Ring in private

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ring of a target just outside the bull
second meaning: personal and not openly shown, as of feelings

explanation.surface: A boxing ring hired for private use.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is the scoring ring next to the bullseye on a target; as an adjective it means private, as in inner thoughts.

clue.text: Clerical dignitary caught out immediately

indicators.note: out means removed or dropped from the word

parts.note: a canon is a member of a cathedral chapter
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is caught out in some wrongdoing straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught out' reads as one phrase, but it splits into C and the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned adverb meaning soon or at once, a literary synonym for immediately.

clue.text: One interrupting beak causes row

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one piece cuts into the middle of another

parts.note: beak is slang for a nose
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone interrupting a magistrate sparks an argument in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is also British slang for a magistrate, which the surface suggests, but here it is the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Row, rhyming with cow, means a din or loud racket, so it is a synonym for noise.

clue.text: Play patience

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slack or allowed variation, as in play in a steering wheel

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads as an instruction to play the card game patience (solitaire), but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering the word means permitted variation or slack in a fit; in general use it means forbearance and patience.

clue.text: Frilly thing, clean item of bedwear

indicators.note: frills are fancy ruffles, suggesting the letters are fussed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
to dress a wound is to clean and bandage it

explanation.surface: A frilly garment, freshly laundered, ready for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frilly' looks like a description of the garment, but it signals the rearrangement of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a loose gown worn by women and girls in bed, so an item of bedwear.

clue.text: Strength of character in Educating Rita

indicators.note: in says the letters are sitting within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words of the title

explanation.surface: Praise for the resilience of the heroine of Educating Rita, Willy Russell's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means courage and resolve, the toughness of character that keeps someone going.
